title: Multifrequency Black Hole Imaging for the Next-generation Event Horizon Telescope
question: How to simultaneously reconstruct interferometric images at multiple frequencies along with their spectral index and curvature maps using Regularized Maximum Likelihood (RML) methods.

what.value: Total flux densities and multi-frequency CLEAN images of HL Tau

evidence.quote: During the eht-imaging procedure, we rescale the total flux density of the intermediate images used for self-calibration to the total flux density values reported in Table 1 of (cite: ALMA_HlTau).
We compare our results to the original images presented in (cite: ALMA_HlTau), which were conducted with multi-frequency CLEAN imaging in CASA (cite: Rau_2011).

what.value: MOJAVE VLBA datasets and CLEAN images at 8.1, 8.4, and 12.1 GHz

evidence.loc: VLBA imaging of MOJAVE data sets
evidence.quote: We then enforced the total flux density at each frequency through self-calibration of the visibility amplitudes using the total flux densities taken from the publicly available MOJAVE images reconstructed with CLEAN.

evidence.loc: VLBA imaging of MOJAVE data sets
evidence.quote: In 12 and 13 we show results for both our simultaneous eht-imaging RML reconstructions and the original CLEAN reconstructions presented in (cite: Hovatta_2014), which were preformed independently at the three frequencies and then aligned.

what.value: Historical atmospheric data from the MERRA-2 database

evidence.quote: We use historical atmospheric data from the MERRA-2 database (cite: Gelaro_2017) as inputs to the am radiative transfer code (cite: Paine_2019),

recipe.goal: Generate synthetic ngEHT multi-frequency data from GRMHD models
recipe.method: Simulate uv-coverage for the proposed ngEHT array, sample the Fourier transform of GRMHD model images (from KORAL/grtrans, BHAC/BHOSS, kharma/ipole), and add thermal noise (using MERRA-2 and am atmospheric model) plus systematic gain and phase errors.
key_parameters: Bandwidth 2 GHz per sub-band, integration time 120 s, quantization efficiency 0.88
Receiver temperatures: 40 K at 86 GHz, 50 K at 230 GHz, 75 K at 345 GHz
assumptions: No frequency phase transfer (FPT) techniques used

recipe.goal: Reconstruct multi-frequency images and spectral maps from synthetic ngEHT and real MOJAVE VLBI data
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit reference image, spectral index map, and spectral curvature map by minimizing the RML objective function first using closure phases and log-closure amplitudes, then self-calibrating once and re-imaging with calibrated visibility amplitudes and closure phases.
key_parameters: Curvature beta=0 for 230 GHz narrow-band ngEHT and MOJAVE reconstructions
assumptions: Good independent measurements of total flux density are available to rescale closure-only images prior to self-calibration

recipe.goal: Average and reconstruct multi-frequency ALMA images and spectral index map of HL Tau
recipe.method: Average ALMA Band 6 and Band 7 complex visibilities across eight spectral windows and in 300 s time windows, then simultaneously fit reference image (at 287 GHz) and spectral index map directly to complex visibilities with three rounds of self-calibration.
key_parameters: Time averaging window = 300 s; reference frequency = 287 GHz; spectral curvature beta = 0; fiducial spectral index alpha_0 = 0
assumptions: Total flux densities rescaled to Table 1 of ALMA Partnership et al. (2015)

answer_key.quantity: HL Tau unresolved spectral index (224 to 351 GHz, eht-imaging)

evidence.quote: This procedure produces an unresolved spectral index $\alpha=2.74$ over the band from 224 to 351 GHz, which matches the reported unresolved spectral index of $\alpha=2.77\pm0.13$ in (cite: ALMA_HlTau).
